topic.title: Proposing __parse__: a standard inverse of __str__
topic.text:
Python standardizes T → str via __str__ , but it does not for the partial inverse str ⇀ T . Given a type and a string, nothing in the standard enables introspection whether the type offers string parsing or how to invoke it. A few constructors oblige, but not all of them are useful, like bool("False") yields True .

I have drafted a PEP proposing an optional class method, __parse__(cls, text: str, /) -> Self , whose presence is the introspectable, overloadable declaration. It requires no changes to syntax, constructors, or serialization formats. The target type is a parameter, so the problems that stopped __json__ / __deserialize__ should not arise.

Draft: pep-parse/pep-9999.rst at main · cr/pep-parse · GitHub

Before pursuing a sponsor, is the problem already recognized in discussions that I can’t find? And do the proposal’s two open questions – dunder versus plain class method, and the strength of the round-trip requirement – have obvious answers I’m not seeing?

reason: Nothing in the graph matches closely. That is not proof the idea is new. Routed to core developers from the nearest earlier forum threads.
